Article Title: PwD car owners get longer FASTag free-pass validity
Article Text:
PwD car owners get longer FASTag free-pass validity (AI-generated image)

NEW DELHI: In a relief to persons with disabilities (PwD) owning cars, govt has extended the validity of exempted FASTags (free pass) from the existing one year to up to five years, depending on the degree of disability. The revised norms will come into effect from Oct 2, Gandhi Jayanti.Vehicles specially designed and built for PwDs, as well as vehicles registered under ownership type “Divyangjan”, under Motor Vehicles Act and rules are exempted from paying user fee on national highways. At present, the validity of such exempted FASTag is one year.In a communication to NHAI, road transport ministry said that under the revised procedure for exempted FASTags for PwDs with 70% to 100% disability will be valid for five years, while those with more than 40% but less than 70% disability will be valid for three years.The ministry has linked the validity of the tags to the percentage of disability recorded in a valid disability certificate, Unique Disability Identity (UDID) card or other applicable records. The tags will be renewed, thereafter, subject to continued eligibility and compliance with National Highways Fee Rules.The ministry said the revised provision was aimed at avoiding recurring procedural requirements for issuance of exempted FASTags to eligible divyangjan/ PwD vehicle owners.
Article Summary: Vehicles specially designed and built for pwds, as well as vehicles registered under ownership type ‘divyangjan’, are exempted from paying user fee on national highways. At present, the validity of such exempted fastag is one year.

Article Title: UPITS 2026 concludes with 4,400 MoUs worth Rs 6,500 crore; business worth Rs 15,500 crore estimated
Article Text:
The event proved to be a concrete and significant milestone towards making the state a one-trillion-dollar economy.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The five-day Uttar Pradesh International Trade Show (UPITS) 2026 concluded on Tuesday with the signing of 4,400 Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs) worth approximately Rs 6,500 crore (around USD 680 million), while potential business worth around Rs 15,500 crore was estimated from business enquiries received during the event.The fourth edition of the trade show was held at the India Expo Centre & Mart from September 25 to 29. Official figures from the Federation of Indian Export Organisations (FIEO) cited in the press release indicated that the event recorded 41,500 B2B and business meetings.Of these, 13,500 meetings took place in the Reverse Buyers-Sellers Meet (RBSM) area, while approximately 28,000 business interactions were recorded in the main exhibition area.Through these meetings, domestic and international buyers directly worked out the framework for long-term business partnerships with the state's entrepreneurs and manufacturers.A total footfall of 5,98,693 visitors and buyers was registered across the five days, comprising 1,74,990 domestic business buyers and 4,23,703 general visitors.The figures represented an increase across key business parameters compared to the 2025 edition.Total B2B meetings increased by 31.12 per cent from 31,650 in 2025 to 41,500 this year. Sessions with foreign buyers in the RBSM section rose by 123.1 per cent from 6,050 to 13,500, while meetings in the main exhibition area grew by 9.38 per cent.The number of MoUs signed rose by 12.82 per cent from 3,900 to 4,400, while their estimated value rose by 142.54 per cent from Rs 2,680 crore (USD 425 million) to Rs 6,500 crore (USD 680 million). Business enquiries also recorded a 24 per cent rise, leading to an estimated potential business increase from Rs 12,500 crore to Rs 15,500 crore.International participation expanded from a single partner country, Russia, in the previous edition to six partner nations this year, namely Russia, Austria, Japan, Singapore, Belarus, and Vietnam. Overseas delegations engaged with sectors including manufacturing, information technology, electronics, textiles, and agri-food processing.Chief minister Yogi Adityanath's ambitious "One District, One Dish (ODOC)" scheme remained the main attraction among foreign and domestic buyers throughout the event. Traditional crafts, handloom products, brass products, carpets, the leather industry and distinctive agricultural products from the state's 75 districts gained direct access to the global market.With MSMEs and local artisans receiving direct orders from international companies, the event's business character proved to be more practical and result-oriented.Overall, the event has proved to be a concrete and significant milestone towards making the state a one-trillion-dollar economy.
Article Summary: The uttar pradesh international trade show (upits) 2026 concluded on tuesday. The fourth edition of the trade show was held at the india expo centre & mart from september 25 to 29. A total footfall of 5,98,693 visitors and buyers was registered across the five days.

Article Title: 15k Ladakh-grown Liliums set out for national flower markets
Article Text:
The consignment comprised 15,000 red, pink, white, and orange Lilium blooms cultivated at an altitude of 10,600ft at the world’s highest flower field at Choglamsar, Leh.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

SRINAGAR: The first consignment of Ladakh-grown Lilium flowers was dispatched to major flower markets in India on Tuesday, in what the Union Territory administration called a major step towards boosting new economic opportunities and entrepreneurship in the cold desert.The consignment comprised 15,000 red, pink, white, and orange Lilium blooms cultivated at an altitude of 10,600ft at the world’s highest flower field at Choglamsar, Leh. These “A-grade” Liliums have four to five buds on each stem and fetch a premium price of around Rs 150-200 in retail markets. The flowers, with a shelf life of five to seven days, will be sold in various domestic markets, primarily Delhi, Mumbai, and Chandigarh.Ladakh lieutenant governor Vinai Kumar Saxena, who flagged off the consignment at Leh airport, said: “This first-of-its-kind high-altitude commercial floriculture project in Ladakh represents a major agricultural and visual shift for the region, which has, since ages, been identified by its rugged mountains and barren valleys. Millions of Liliums have added a vibrant contrast to this dull landscape.”Saxena said the “historic” initiative had emerged as a powerful economic tool for creating alternative sustainable livelihoods in Ladakh.Fifteen women cut, sort and package the flowers at these fields for a daily wage of Rs 900 each. A young, qualified botanist markets the produce to flower markets across the nation. The employees are all locals.The UT administration has directed deputy commissioners of Kargil, Drass, Sham, Changthang and Zanskar districts to replicate the high-altitude floriculture model by identifying at least 20 acres of land in each district.The flower field in Leh, which houses more than 25 lakh blooms, was developed and readied within just two months. It was opened to the public on Sept 17 this year and has since received an overwhelming response from visitors.
Article Summary: The consignment comprised 15,000 red, pink, white, and orange lilium blooms cultivated at the world’s highest flower field at choglamsar, leh. The flowers, with a shelf life of five to seven days, will be sold in various domestic markets, primarily delhi, mumbai and chandigarh.

Article Title: Serena Williams’ new business move puts the next trillion-dollar company in focus
Article Text:
Serena Williams explains Starfire Ventures’ new direction

Serena Williams is thinking beyond billion-dollar businesses

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Serena Williams is no longer treating business as a side project. The tennis legend has turned her investment operation into a serious force in venture capital, recently rebranding Serena Ventures as Starfire Ventures. The firm now has 16 unicorns in its portfolio, while Williams says its ambition extends far beyond the next billion-dollar company. Her focus is finding overlooked founders, backing businesses with major potential and building a firm that can outlast her own name. At the same time, Williams is balancing investing with motherhood and a selective return to professional tennis.The rebrand from Serena Ventures to Starfire Ventures marks a deliberate change in how Williams sees the business. She said the original name worked, but she wanted the firm to become something larger than its founder.“We’ve just rebranded ourselves. . . . I felt like Serena Ventures is great, but I wanted it to be bigger than me. There are so many amazing people on the team, and there’s so much that we do. I felt like when you put a name on something, it can limit what you do. I want it to live on. I want this to be something that people look at years and years from now .. .”Williams says her approach to investing is driven mostly by a clear philosophy, with instinct also playing a role. Her firm has backed 16 companies that have reached unicorn status, giving the former world No. 1 a growing track record outside sport.She also pushes back against the idea that investing in women and underrepresented founders is simply a social exercise.“We invest in everyone. We invest in people who look like you. We invest in people who look like me. It’s just that we do see a lot of women and a lot of underrepresented founders because they know that we’ll hear their story. And we don’t invest in all of them. . . . We are only investing in winners. If we don’t feel the company is going to return our fund, we’re not going to invest in them. That’s just how we look at it.”Williams sees an investment gap as an opportunity. She believes some founders are overlooked because investors do not always recognise their potential early enough.Her long-term goal is clear. “We’re thinking about the next billion-dollar company, the next trillion-dollar company, and how to be on those cap tables as well.”That ambition sits alongside a very structured personal life. Williams said she spends about 90% of her professional time with Starfire Ventures when she is not focused on her children.Her return to tennis is also carefully managed. Rather than pursuing another Grand Slam run, she has chosen a limited schedule that fits around her family and business commitments.“I’m not going back out there to win Grand Slams. I have a full-time job. But this is what I’m willing to do, and this is how I’m willing to show up.”For Williams, the next phase is not about choosing between tennis, business and family. It is about setting firm boundaries and deciding exactly where her time matters most.
Article Summary: Serena williams is no longer treating business as a side project. The tennis legend has turned her investment operation into a serious force in venture capital. She recently rebranded serena ventures as starfire ventures. The firm now has 16 unicorns in its portfolio. Williams says its ambition extends far beyond the next billion-dollar company.

The bottom line

Bharat NCAP 2.0, planned for October 2027, will look beyond what happens when a car crashes. The proposed system will examine the entire safety chain: from how a vehicle helps avoid a collision to how well it protects occupants, pedestrians and other vulnerable road users, and what happens after an accident.Union road transport and highways minister Nitin Gadkari announced the proposed timeline at the SIAM Annual Convention in September. The second phase is being planned as the first phase of Bharat New Car Assessment Programme, or Bharat NCAP, approaches the end of its current cycle.According to the ministry of road transport and highways’ draft AIS-197 Revision 1, the first phase of Bharat NCAP began on October 1, 2023 and is valid until September 30, 2027. The draft revision has been prepared as the framework for Bharat NCAP 2.0.The proposed changes could make the safety rating a much broader measure of a car’s performance, not just in a crash, but before, during and after one.Bharat NCAP is India’s own vehicle crash-testing and safety-rating programme. It was formally launched by the ministry of road transport and highways in August 2023 and became operational from October 1, 2023.The programme applies to type-approved passenger vehicles in the M1 category with a gross vehicle weight of less than 3.5 tonnes. It is voluntary, which means manufacturers can offer eligible vehicles for assessment.The programme is anchored by the Central Institute of Road Transport (CIRT), while testing is carried out through designated agencies with the required infrastructure.At its core, Bharat NCAP gives car buyers a common safety benchmark. A vehicle must already meet mandatory regulatory requirements to be sold in India. Bharat NCAP goes a step further by putting eligible vehicles through specified tests and awarding them a rating of between one and five stars.The idea is fairly simple: instead of looking only at a car’s price, design or features, buyers get an additional reference point to understand how the vehicle performs in standardised safety tests.The government has also positioned the programme as a way to encourage manufacturers to improve vehicle safety and strengthen the safety standards of cars made in India.The existing programme broadly assesses three areas:Vehicles are subjected to prescribed crash tests and other assessments. Their performance across these parameters is then used to arrive at the overall star rating.The current framework includes a 64 kmph offset frontal impact test, a 50 kmph side movable deformable barrier test and a pole side impact test, among other checks prescribed under AIS-197.The assessment therefore goes beyond simply asking whether the passenger compartment remains intact.Adult Occupant Protection examines the risk of injury to adults in different crash conditions and seating positions. Child Occupant Protection looks at the protection offered to younger passengers, including the use and installation of child restraint systems.Safety Assist Technologies, meanwhile, covers technologies designed to help prevent crashes or reduce their severity.A car may offer different levels of protection to adults and children, so Bharat NCAP evaluates the two separately.The adult assessment focuses on occupant protection during prescribed crash scenarios, while the child assessment considers how effectively younger occupants are protected and how child restraint systems work within the vehicle.This also means that a car’s overall star rating is not simply a score from one crash test. It reflects performance across several safety parameters.For consumers, the individual scores can therefore provide more information than looking at the star rating alone.Bharat NCAP is anchored by CIRT, with testing carried out through designated testing agencies that have the required facilities.The wider automotive testing ecosystem includes agencies such as the Automotive Research Association of India (ARAI) and the International Centre for Automotive Technology (ICAT).Manufacturers submit eligible vehicles for assessment under the programme. The existing framework specifies procedures around the variant selected for testing, including provisions concerning the base variant of a model.That distinction matters when reading a Bharat NCAP result. A rating should not automatically be assumed to apply to every variant of a model unless the official assessment covers those variants.Bharat NCAP ratings range from one to five stars. A higher rating indicates stronger performance under the programme’s prescribed assessment criteria.But a five-star rating is not a guarantee that occupants will escape injury in every real-world crash. NCAP testing is conducted under standardised conditions and is intended to provide a basis for comparing vehicle safety performance.It is also important to distinguish Bharat NCAP from the mandatory certification requirements for selling a vehicle in India.Bharat NCAP is voluntary and is designed to provide consumers with additional information beyond the mandatory regulatory framework. A vehicle being tested or rated under Bharat NCAP should therefore not be confused with regulatory approval.Since its launch, Bharat NCAP has increasingly become part of the safety conversation around new car launches. The ratings have also become a factor in how manufacturers present their vehicles to consumers, particularly as safety becomes a more visible consideration in the passenger-vehicle market.This is where the proposed second phase takes a much wider approach.The draft AIS-197 Revision 1 divides Bharat NCAP 2.0 into five safety verticals:The change is significant because the current system focuses mainly on occupant protection and safety-assist technologies, while the proposed framework looks at the complete safety chain.The draft framework uses a 100-point assessment structure, with Crash Protection accounting for 55% of the assessment. The remaining weightage covers the other safety areas.In other words, the crash itself will still be a major part of the rating, but it will no longer be the only part of the safety story.Bharat NCAP 2.0 proposes expanding the Crash Protection assessment to five mandatory crash tests:Adult and child occupant protection will continue to be assessed separately.The addition of full-width frontal and rear-impact tests means the proposed system will examine crash scenarios beyond the core tests in the existing framework.That gives the second phase a wider testing footprint and allows different types of impacts to form part of the overall safety assessment.One of the biggest differences in Bharat NCAP 2.0 is that the programme is designed to look at what happens before a crash as well.Crash Avoidance is one of the five proposed verticals. It focuses on technologies and vehicle characteristics that can help prevent a collision or reduce its severity.Safe Driving is another proposed category, widening the assessment beyond the vehicle’s passive protection features.Together, these categories shift the focus from simply asking, “How well does this car perform when it crashes?” to a broader question: “How does this vehicle contribute to safety across different stages of a road incident?”Bharat NCAP 2.0 also proposes a separate Vulnerable Road User Protection category. This brings pedestrians and other vulnerable road users more directly into the safety assessment.Post-Crash Safety is one of the five proposed assessment areas. Minister Gadkari described Bharat NCAP 2.0 as covering the entire safety chain, including post-crash evacuation and care. “We are going to evaluate the entire crash chain,” Gadkari said, adding that new technologies developed globally as well as by startups would be considered under the programme.This means the assessment is intended to extend beyond the instant of impact and examine safety considerations in the period immediately after a crash.It adds another layer to the programme’s approach: avoiding the crash where possible, protecting people during the impact, and addressing safety after the collision.For buyers, Bharat NCAP offers an additional way to compare cars beyond mandatory safety requirements.A consumer can look at a vehicle’s overall rating as well as its adult and child protection performance and the safety technologies considered in the assessment.The rating is not meant to replace other factors involved in buying a car. Price, size, fuel efficiency, features, driving requirements and other considerations remain relevant, but the proposed 2.0 framework would expand that information further.Buyers could eventually have a broader picture of how a car performs across crash protection, crash avoidance, safe driving, vulnerable-road-user protection and post-crash safety.Bharat NCAP is one part of a much larger road-safety challenge, focusing on the structure of vehicles. Vehicle design and safety technology can influence the outcome of a crash, but they cannot address every reason why accidents happen.The ministry has identified several factors associated with road crashes, including speeding, mobile-phone use, drunken driving, wrong-side driving, lane indiscipline, jumping red lights and failure to use helmets and seat belts. Vehicle condition, road conditions and weather can also play a role.Government data recorded 1,68,491 road accident fatalities in 2022.Bharat NCAP therefore addresses one part of this wider equation: the safety performance of vehicles. Its proposed second phase would broaden that role by looking at what a vehicle can do to help avoid crashes, how it protects people when a crash occurs, how it protects vulnerable road users and what happens afterwards.The current Bharat NCAP phase remains valid until September 30, 2027. The government has proposed introducing Bharat NCAP 2.0 from October 2027, with the draft AIS-197 Revision 1 serving as the framework for the next phase.The proposed transition would take India’s vehicle safety-rating system from a relatively focused crash and occupant-protection programme to a broader safety assessment.The familiar one-to-five-star rating would remain the consumer-facing language of vehicle safety, but the assessment behind it is set to become much more comprehensive.The bigger shift is in the question Bharat NCAP is trying to answer. Instead of looking only at how a car performs when it is involved in a crash, the proposed system would examine the vehicle’s safety journey from avoiding a collision to protecting occupants and vulnerable road users, and supporting safety after the crash.That could give Indian car buyers a wider set of safety information to consider when choosing their next vehicle.
Article Summary: Bharat ncap is india’s own vehicle crash-testing and safety-rating programme. First phase began on october 1, 2023 and is valid until september 30, 2027. The proposed system will examine the entire safety chain: from how a vehicle helps avoid a collision to how well it protects occupants.

Article Title: Google data center head says that there are 'hundreds of thousands' of skilled trade jobs across the US as the company launches commitment to help 25,000 ...
Article Text:
A personal story behind the push

What the commitment includes

Why the need is so urgent

Part of a broader pattern of investment

Google has announced a major initiative to help 25,000 US veterans and military families transition into skilled trade careers, as demand for electricians, pipefitters, and project managers surges amid the AI-driven data center boom. Tim Chadwick, Google’s Data Center Operations Area Lead, says there are “hundreds of thousands” of skilled trade jobs open across the country right now. Data centers have become central to the AI economy, requiring massive investment and labor. Google estimates that hundreds of thousands of skilled trade roles are currently unfilled across the U.S., ranging from master electricians to project managers. These jobs offer long-term stability and high wages, but employers face challenges in recruiting due to decades of emphasis on four-year degrees over vocational training.The announcement was written by Tim Chadwick, Google's Data Center Operations Area lead for Ohio and Indiana, who shared his own path from military service into the tech industry. Chadwick spent seven years as a nuclear-trained operator in the US Navy and another 13 years as a submarine officer before transitioning to civilian life — a shift he described as genuinely difficult, one he credits his professional network with helping him navigate.A former shipmate ultimately helped him land an interview for a role managing data center engineering operations.Chadwick noted that many of the skills built while running a nuclear submarine — planning and leading a mission, working closely with technicians, and exercising sound judgment under pressure — translate directly into overseeing data center operations, a connection that shaped his interest in helping other veterans find similar paths.Google.org's funding and support will flow to three organizations with deep experience serving the veteran community: Hiring Our Heroes, Student Veterans of America (SVA), and the Home Builders Institute (HBI). Together, these organizations will offer hands-on pre-apprenticeships, career coaching, and direct job placement support aimed at helping veterans and military family members move into skilled trade careers.Chadwick pointed to the sheer scale of unmet demand driving the initiative, noting that hundreds of thousands of skilled trade roles are currently open across the US, spanning positions like master electrician, lead pipefitter, and project manager. He described these as high-growth careers offering long-term financial stability — and argued that veterans and military families are especially well-suited for them, given how closely the roles align with skills many already carry from military service, including problem-solving under pressure, teamwork, and a strong drive to get a job done right.This isn't Google's first move in this space. Earlier this year, the company joined BlackRock, Ford, and Carhartt to launch the Alliance for America's Skilled Trades, aimed at building stronger pipelines into vocational careers nationally. Google.org has also previously funded the Electrical Training Alliance (etA) to bring AI-powered learning tools directly onto the trade floor, and provided a $4 million grant to Student Veterans of America to expand access to Google Career Certificates and AI training for veterans nationwide.Today's announcement is also part of Google.org's broader AI Opportunity Fund for the United States, an initiative aimed at ensuring Americans across different career paths can benefit from advances in AI technology, rather than being left behind by them.
Article Summary: Google has announced a major initiative to help 25,000 us veterans and military families transition into skilled trade careers. The move comes as demand for electricians, pipefitters, and project managers surges amid the ai-driven data center boom. Google estimates that hundreds of thousands of skilled trade roles are currently unfilled across the u.s.

Article Title: Apple Pay launches in India; here's how to set it up and where you can use it
Article Text:
Apple Pay launched in India: How it works, and who can use it

How to set up and use Apple Pay

Where you can use it

Apple has officially launched Apple Pay in India. With this launch the company brings its secure and seamless payment system to iPhone, iPad and Apple Watch users, with Mac support coming soon. Apple Pay roll out in the country will enable users to pay in stores, apps, and on the web without typing PINs and OTPs marking a significant milestone in India’s fast-growing digital payments ecosystem. At launch, Apple Pay supports Axis Bank-issued Visa and Mastercard credit cards, enabling payments at thousands of merchants across India and anywhere NFC transactions are accepted globally.Apple also emphasised that privacy remains central to how Apple Pay functions. When a card is added, the actual card number is never stored on the device or Apple's servers, nor shared with merchants during a transaction. Instead, the system assigns a unique Device Account Number, which is encrypted and stored securely within the device's Secure Element — a certified, industry-standard chip built specifically to protect payment information.Presently, Apple Pay is exclusively available to customers holding Axis Bank-issued Visa and Mastercard credit cards, letting them add those cards to Apple Pay and use them at thousands of in-store and online merchants across India, as well as anywhere that accepts NFC transactions.Jennifer Bailey, Apple's vice president of Apple Pay and Apple Wallet, framed the launch as a natural fit for India's fast-growing digital economy, pointing to the country's dynamic, digitally savvy population that's increasingly embracing cashless payments while expecting strong security and privacy standards. She described Apple Pay's core value proposition as making everyday card payments easy, secure, and private — from a simple tap in stores without needing a separate app, PIN, or OTP, to checking out online without repeatedly re-entering payment details.Apple Pay is easy to set up. Customers can add a card directly to Apple Wallet via the latest version of the Axis Bank app. Alternatively, simply open the Wallet app on iPhone, tap the plus sign, and follow the steps to add an eligible card. Once a user adds a card to their Apple device, they can start using Apple Pay right away.Using Apple Pay in stores is seamless and easy. Simply double-click the side button or Home button; authenticate using Face ID, Touch ID, or a device passcode if prompted; and hold the top of the iPhone or display of the Apple Watch near the contactless reader to pay. When using Apple Pay, users will continue to earn the rewards and benefits offered by their cards.At launch, Apple Pay will be accepted at millions of merchants across India, including Apple Store locations, Blinkit, Chaayos, Comet, Croma, Interflora, Ixigo, Le15 Patisserie, Reliance brands, Tata 1mg, and Zomato, among others. Apple has also partnered with several payment service providers, including Cashfree, JusPay, Mswipe, Paytm, PayU, Pine Labs, Razorpay, and Worldline, to extend Apple Pay's reach across their respective merchant networks, with more merchants and apps expected to be added over time.Globally, Apple Pay is now available in more than 90 countries and regions, working with over 11,000 bank and network partners worldwide — making India one of the more prominent recent additions to that global rollout.
Article Summary: Apple has officially launched apple pay in india. With this launch the company brings its secure and seamless payment system to iphone, ipad and apple watch users, with mac support coming soon. Apple pay roll out in the country will enable users to pay in stores, apps, and on the web without typing pins and otps.

Article Title: Anthropic warns AI may pose ‘existential risks to humanity’ in IPO filing
Article Text:
Anthropic

Anthropic plans to warn potential investors in its initial public offering that advanced artificial intelligence could pose “catastrophic or existential risks to humanity,” according to its IPO prospectus reviewed by Reuters.The filing says its AI models could exhibit “self-preserving behaviours,” including attempts to “resist shutdown,” “conceal or manipulate information” and behaviour “resembling blackmail”. “Our development of highly advanced models, platforms, and applications and expansion of use cases could further increase the risk that our models cause harm,” Anthropic said.The company, which positions itself as a safety-first AI lab, devoted 80 pages of prospectus’s 261-page main body to risks, nearly twice the 48 pages describing its business. SpaceX, which owns xAI, devoted about 38 of 277 pages to risks.Anthropic said models could develop unexpected capabilities during training that might be discovered only after deployment and had resulted in significant safety incidents. It also warned that models might recognise evaluations and modify their behaviour, limiting safety assessments. Researchers have similarly warned that increasingly capable models can recognise when they are being watched and adjust their behaviour, complicating monitoring.Anthropic and other developers, including OpenAI, have faced scrutiny after experimental systems defied constraints, including a reported breach of Australia’s health-system database by an OpenAI model. Anthropic safety researcher Evan Hubinger estimated a greater than 10% probability that AI could kill humans within the next decade, echoing former colleague Jacob Coxon.Despite emphasising safety, Anthropic said returns on such investment were unclear and did not disclose its spending. Earlier this month, it said safety work used about 6% of its AI research computing power during a sample week in July. It called safety efforts “resource-intensive” and said limited funds must be divided among computing power, costly AI talent and safety.The Claude developer said customer usage and revenue depended on new models and that a “continuous and overlapping cadence” of releases was “inherent to remaining at the frontier of AI development.” Last week, it released a new Opus model, 10 days after CEO Dario Amodei published a nearly 4,000-word essay urging the frontier to be paced.Anthropic has pledged to publish more data on its use of AI models to build future generations as experts warn about recursive self-improvement, when models develop without human help. Anthropic declined to comment. Analysts said slowing down could hand rivals an advantage. Anthropic declined to comment in response to a request for comment.
Article Summary: Anthropic plans to warn potential investors in its initial public offering that advanced artificial intelligence could pose “catastrophic or existential risks to humanity” the company, which positions itself as a safety-first ai lab, devoted 80 pages of prospectus’s 261-page main body to risks.

Article Title: AT&T CEO John Stankey 'agrees' with T-Mobile CEO Peter Osvaldik that Elon Musk's plans to shake up mobile industry with Starlink should be laughed out of the room
Article Text:
What T-Mobile CEO Peter Osvaldik said first

AT&T CEO John Stankey's rebuttal: Fiber beats satellite, full stop

Why the rivalry is heating up

The scale of Starlink's ambitions

Why Stankey says the math doesn't work

AT&T CEO John Stankey has sided with T-Mobile’s chief executive Peter Osvaldik in rejecting Elon Musk ’s plan to disrupt the mobile industry with Starlink. Speaking to Axios, Stankey said SpaceX ’s proposal to turn its satellite business into a global competitor to traditional telecom networks is “not a viable strategy.” He argued that fiber infrastructure remains superior, noting AT&T’s $3 billion deal with Corning to expand its fiber footprint. Earlier this month, T-Mobile CEO Peter Osvaldik dismissed Musk’s Starlink ambitions outright, and said that the strategy should be “laughed out of the room. ” Osvaldik said Starlink’s approach lacked the scale and economics to compete with established carriers, reinforcing skepticism across the telecom industry.T-Mobile CFO Peter Osvaldik was blunt in his own assessment of Starlink's mobile ambitions, saying that "everybody in the know" is laughing at parts of the plan, and describing SpaceX's proposal as something that isn't fathomable from a technical standpoint. He argued Starlink doesn't represent a real competitive threat from a wireless perspective, pointing to basic physics as the core obstacle: satellite signals, he said, can't penetrate buildings, walls, or even something as simple as a car windshield, making Starlink's direct-to-cell ambitions far less practical in dense urban environments than in the remote areas where satellite coverage genuinely shines.Speaking to Axios, Stankey made a similarly confident case for why AT&T isn't worried, backing it with a major infrastructure move. AT&T announced a $3 billion deal with Corning this week to expand its fiber infrastructure, arguing that fiber delivers speeds three times faster than satellite technology. Stankey didn't mince words about the comparison, saying nothing beats fiber, and that even if satellite technology performs at its absolute best over the next decade, it still won't be able to match what fiber delivers.The pushback from both carriers comes as Musk and SpaceX President Gwynne Shotwell have been increasingly vocal about turning Starlink into a genuine competitor to traditional phone and internet providers. Starlink already competes with legacy telecom companies for home and business internet customers, and the company has now started talking openly about a mobile business that would put it in direct competition with wireless carriers.Shotwell added fuel to that narrative in August, during SpaceX's first earnings call as a public company, predicting that SpaceX would be able to win over a meaningful number of customers from existing carriers because its service would simply be better. That comment rattled markets, sending shares of AT&T, Verizon, and T-Mobile lower the following day.As of June 30, Starlink had 12 million subscribers and more than 10,200 satellites providing coverage across 167 countries, according to SpaceX's first earnings report as a public company. While SpaceX's rockets and AI work tend to dominate headlines, its connectivity business is actually the company's largest revenue driver, accounting for 55% of total sales.Becoming a genuine fourth major US mobile carrier, however, would require significantly more terrestrial infrastructure to match the capacity of a traditional cellular network — a build-out one analyst estimated could cost SpaceX more than $100 billion. SpaceX believes it has found a cheaper alternative: installing small cellular base stations alongside Starlink dishes at homes and businesses, adding capacity where satellite coverage alone falls short, without needing to build the kind of sprawling cell tower network traditional carriers rely on. Musk has claimed these small stations could eventually deliver connectivity to phones with better and higher bandwidth than what's currently available from existing cellular providers.Stankey pushed back hard on that plan's feasibility, arguing that installing enough small stations to match a traditional network's capacity would cost roughly the same as simply building a full macro cellular network. He also pointed to a significant regulatory hurdle: current law doesn't allow companies to radiate cellular signals from someone's home without their permission, unless that law changes. He suggested that if the approach were genuinely viable and cost-effective, AT&T would already be installing similar antennas across its own massive existing fiber network.
Article Summary: At&t ceo john stankey says spacex's starlink plan is "not a viable strategy" he argued that fiber infrastructure remains superior, noting at&t’s $3 billion deal with corning to expand its fiber footprint. Earlier this month, t-mobile ceo peter osvaldik said starlink's approach lacked the scale and economics to compete with established carriers.

Article Title: In 2005, two Vancouver writers ate only food produced within 100 miles to reconnect with local farms; they held the rule for a full year, with salt as the one exception
Article Text:
Sole Food Street Farms planter boxes located at Hawks and Hastings Avenue (Strathcona location) in Vancouver. Image credits: Wikimedia Commons

The 100-mile rule, March 21, 2005 to March 20, 2006

Foods given up: sugar, Cheerios, olive oil, rice and beer

Food-miles study, 2008: transport 11 percent of emissions, production 83 percent

Salt farmers harvesting salt. Image credits: Wikimedia Commons

USDA report, 2010: no generally accepted definition of local food

After March 2006:

farmers' markets

, a community garden plot and winter preserving

On March 21, 2005, Vancouver writers Alisa Smith and J.B. MacKinnon began a year-long experiment. They would buy food and drink for home consumption only if it had been produced within 100 miles of their Vancouver apartment. Grist reported that they completed the trial on March 20, 2006. The experiment drew heavy media attention. Grist reported that the couple's column about the 100-Mile Diet, first published on TheTyee.ca, attracted about 40,000 readers and was linked, reprinted and blogged about across the internet. "This is what it's like to witness the birth of a movement," MacKinnon said, and the couple soon launched the website 100MileDiet.org. Salt was the one known exception to their rule, and their book ends with a trip to Bamfield, where they boiled down seawater to make their own salt.Their 100-mile circle was centered on their Vancouver apartment. The Tyee began publishing their series on June 28, 2005, and described it in a 2020 retrospective as a series that sparked a global phenomenon. The same retrospective noted that "locavore" was named 2007 Word of the Year by the New Oxford American Dictionary.The book's description lists sugar, Cheerios, olive oil, rice, Pizza Pops and beer among the foods the couple did without. A 2008 Washington Post review of their memoir, Plenty, noted that they started with little gardening expertise, little money and little access to grocery stores selling local food. In a 2007 Grist interview, Smith said wheat was a big surprise for her. She explained that locally grown wheat flour was hard to find because wheat was traditionally grown on the West Coast before specialization shifted production to the prairie areas. Until they found locally milled flour, Smith said, they were unintentionally following the Atkins Diet.They made judgment calls about production methods. Smith said they accepted eggs from the UBC farm because they knew how the hens were raised and fed. MacKinnon said they accepted vegetables from non-organic growers after learning what the growers had applied and when. He also said local seafood was surprisingly difficult to obtain, despite their location at the mouth of a major salmon river. Even so, he called it the most varied year of eating either of them had ever had.Salt was the one item in their cabinets that did not come from what they called home. The Last Bastille's review noted that the first meal described in the book had only one non-local ingredient, salt from a bag from Oregon, several hundred miles away. In a 2020 interview with The Tyee, MacKinnon said the story ends with a visit to Bamfield, where they boiled seawater to make salt, and that he would now buy salt from Vancouver Island Salt Co. in Black Creek.The study Food-Miles and the Relative Climate Impacts of Food Choices in the United States, published in Environmental Science & Technology in 2008, reported that food travels 1,640 kilometers (1,020 miles) on average for final delivery and 6,760 kilometers across the life-cycle supply chain. Even so, production accounted for 83 percent of the average American household's food-related greenhouse gas emissions. Transportation as a whole made up 11 percent, and final delivery from producer to retail only 4 percent.The authors found that shifting less than one day per week's worth of calories from red meat and dairy products to chicken, fish, eggs or a vegetable-based diet would cut more emissions than buying all food locally. The research covered the average American household, not Smith and MacKinnon specifically. Grist noted that the diet began as an effort to reduce dependence on the fossil fuels used by the conventional food system, then grew into an exploration of community, seasons and flavor.The USDA Economic Research Service report Local Food Systems: Concepts, Impacts, and Issues found no generally accepted definition of local in terms of the distance between production and consumption. The report also found that local food systems made up only a tiny fraction of US agricultural output, even though their share was growing. It noted that small farmers earned more from direct-to-consumer sales than larger farmers did, and it found conflicting evidence on local food's contribution to development, nutrition and greenhouse gas reductions.Direct sales from farmers to consumers made up only 0.4 percent of all agricultural sales in 2007, a narrow measure of local food. The report identified limits to the sector's growth, including the small capacity of farms and the lack of systems to deliver local foods to traditional markets. Its evidence on the effects of local food on the economy, health and nutrition was inconsistent.Grist reported that after the year the couple planned to keep shopping at farmers' markets, tend their community garden plot and preserve local produce for the winter. MacKinnon said their first meal after the experiment was potatoes and eggs, and that they went out for Indian food later that night. Beer, chocolate, olives, lemons and olive oil returned to their diet, but he said some of the foods they had given up did not come back.
Article Summary: Vancouver writers alisa smith and j.b. mackinnon began a year-long experiment. They would buy food and drink only if it had been produced within 100 miles of their apartment. Salt was the one known exception to their rule, and their book ends with a trip to bamfield.

Article Title: In 2007, a Colorado photographer placed cameras on shrinking glaciers; 15 years later, his archive held 1.5 million images now used to measure ice loss
Article Text:
Representative image of a glacier. (Image Credits: Pexels).

The evolution of continuous time-lapse photography

The New Yorker

Representative image of a photographer capturing glacier. (Image Credit: Pexels)

The painstaking task of archiving and its challenges

An extensive collection of 1.5 million images in time-lapse chronicling 15 years of global glacier retreat has been officially preserved and archived at the National Snow and Ice Data Center (NSIDC) . James Balog, an environmental photographer and mountaineer, founded the Extreme Ice Survey (EIS) in 2007. The project aimed to capture the physical impacts of climate change in real-time across the world's most remote frozen environments. The massive repository was transferred via a physical hard drive to the NSIDC server systems at the University of Colorado Boulder. Now the project is a public domain research resource for glaciologists and climate scientists worldwide.Balog’s massive visual census is an expansion of his earlier works, documenting deforestation and endangered wildlife during his global travels. After hearing from others about weather changes, he discerned that the real story was to be found in the ice. With his background in earth science and master’s degree in geomorphology from the Institute for Arctic and Alpine Research (INSTAAR), he felt equipped to track changes in the cryosphere. Balog drew inspiration from photojournalists Robert Capa and W. Eugene Smith, who exposed societal crises, and hoped to bring the same focus to the natural world.The blueprint for the project was conceived during a 2005 assignment forin Iceland, where Balog was taking pictures of crumbling glacial termini (the locations where glaciers meet land or open water). He realized that static single-frame photography wasn’t enough to capture the continuous structural ice loss, leading him to come up with an automated, long-term monitoring system. In partnership with leading glaciologists Tad Pfeffer and Jason Box, he began building time-lapse systems that were encased in custom boxes and powered by solar arrays and car batteries.The technical construction initially occupied Balog’s residential garage, where his family provided assistance. His wife, Suzanne, and daughters, Simone and Emily, were all supportive, with his six-year-old daughter Emily assisting with pieces of equipment like turnbuckles.While Balog’s initial plan was to place 25 time-lapse cameras near the glaciers, the project expanded into a network of 70 cameras stationed in Alaska, Iceland, Greenland, Nepal, Austria, Antarctica, Canada, South Georgia Island and Glacier National Park in Montana. Each camera was programmed to take pictures of glaciers continuously around the clock for months and even years. This helped in creating an extensive database of physical changes on nearly every observed glacier.When Balog initially approached NSIDC while the project was ongoing, talks fell through because he wanted to put a restriction on access for education and non-profit use. Following the conclusion of field operations in 2022, Balog circled back to the institution and agreed to an open science framework.However, transferring the data proved difficult from the start because Balog’s team lacked the bandwidth to push 1.5 million images to NSIDC’s servers and directories were too large; what they needed was funds. Donna Scott, programs and projects lead, secured endorsements from the science team, and director Mark Serreze and Jennifer Kay, a CIRES associate director, stepped up to contribute funding. The transfer then happened by hand in a parking lot, where Scott was handed a military ammunition box containing Balog’s hard drive of 1.5 million images from the EIS project.Once the drive arrived, a dedicated team spent 60 hours downloading, reconciling and organizing the images, including removing more than 200,000 duplicate files. Reflecting on the data transfer, Balog said he wanted to show future generations that some people were paying attention.
Article Summary: 1.5 million images in time-lapse chronicling 15 years of global glacier retreat have been officially preserved and archived at the national snow and ice data center (nsidc) james balog, an environmental photographer and mountaineer, founded the extreme ice survey (eis) in 2007.

Article Title: Pakistan goes bananas over giant gorillas dancing to Bollywood songs
Article Text:
Clips of these larger-than-life performers have been spreading rapidly online (Photo: AFP)

Pakistanis are going bananas over a trend that has crossed the Indian border: Giant gorillas, dancing to Bollywood music.Clips of these larger-than-life performers have been spreading rapidly online, turning them into the surprise stars of weddings, birthdays and other festivities.In the videos, guests can be seen joining in alongside the costumed entertainers, many of them visibly delighted by the unusual addition to their celebrations. The performers swing their oversized arms to pounding DJ tracks while partygoers gather round and dance, creating a lively, comic spectacle that has quickly drawn attention across social media.Behind the trend in Lahore is Shayen Zahoor, who runs Gorilla.co.pk, a business offering giant dancing gorilla acts for events across the city.Speaking to AFP, Zahoor explained how quickly the idea took off. He said the costume was ordered in early April and arrived by the end of the same month, after which the team wasted no time putting it to use.Once the suit arrived, he and his team lost no time getting started."We uploaded a reel on Instagram, and within just two days it reached a million views," Zahoor recalled.The overwhelming response convinced them to treat the venture as a serious business, and bookings soon began pouring in, with the public reaction proving remarkably enthusiastic."On the very first day, we received approximately 1,200 to 1,300 messages," he said, describing how curious would-be customers flooded his inbox.Many wanted to know whether the costume had genuinely arrived, what it would cost to book, and other practical details before making up their minds.What began as a single Instagram reel has since snowballed into a full-fledged entertainment phenomenon, with giant gorillas now a familiar, if unlikely, fixture at Pakistani celebrations.
Article Summary: Pakistanis are going bananas over a trend that has crossed the indian border: giant gorillas, dancing to bollywood music. Clips of these larger-than-life performers have been spreading rapidly online. The performers swing their oversized arms to pounding dj tracks while partygoers gather round and dance.

Article Title: Meet Ben O'Connor, the 16-year-old who sold 200,000 gift boxes before building an app to help farmers manage their work
Article Text:
PC: Linkedln

How did Ben O'Connor sell 200,000 gift boxes at 16

How will FarmFlow work offline on farmers' phones

Ben O'Connor, aged 16, from a dairy farming family in Co. Down, is already a serial entrepreneur. He set up his first business, a firewood venture, at 11, and at 13 founded Giftery, a mail-order gift basket business that went on to sell 200,000 gift boxes within three years. His latest project, FarmFlow, is farm management software he plans to make available for free, with a free tier always on offer. In an interview with Agriland, Ben O'Connor said: "This year I set up FarmFlow." The product is in a "long soft launch" and will relaunch in August with offline use.Agriland reports that O'Connor's first "major" business was Giftery, a mail-order gift basket venture. It was set up when he was 13, and it went on to sell 200,000 units within three years.Running the business came with challenges. "It can be hard to get respect when you're a lot younger than the people you're going into meetings with," O'Connor said. Agriland adds that the Giftery experience did teach him to "not give up".On his latest project, O'Connor said: "This year I set up FarmFlow." According to Agriland, the product aims to manage tasks for farmers or, in his words, "to try to solve problems with a farm".He named issues as wide-ranging as relief milkers, feed rations and livestock weight tracking, saying "there's no real thing that brings them together".He said FarmFlow "learns over time" and is "intended to adapt towards the farm". The product is in its early stages but is usable at present, and farmers are invited to take part in a "long soft launch". O'Connor said: "The system can hold only so many, so we're sort of trying to keep numbers limited while we further test it." He added that, once it is fully launched, "anyone who wants it, we would be more than happy to have them".One planned feature is offline use. O'Connor said the app is currently web-based for demos but will relaunch in August, working offline with data stored locally within the phone. He said operational data is encrypted and "never leaves end-to-end encryption", adding: "We're figuring out how to make it better."O'Connor plans for FarmFlow to be "completely free", though there will be "revenue models in it". He said: "There'll always be a free tier available because I understand the problems that many farms have with cash flow." Agriland reports that paid-for features are planned for the full launch. O'Connor also has his GCSEs ahead of him and an apprenticeship starting in September, but says FarmFlow remains "a priority". "I'm just trying to balance those things at the moment," he said, adding: "I'll always be entrepreneurial."
Article Summary: Ben o'connor, aged 16, from a dairy farming family in co. down, is already a serial entrepreneur. At 13 he founded giftery, a mail-order gift basket business that went on to sell 200,000 gift boxes within three years. His latest project, farmflow, is farm management software he plans to make available for free, with a free tier always on offer.

Article Title: In 1901, Germany opened a “flying train” above the Wupper valley; 125 years later, it carries over 80,000 passengers daily
Article Text:
PC: WSW official press release

Why Germany built the “flying train” above the Wupper valley

How Wuppertal is celebrating 125 years of its “flying train”

PC: WSW official press release

How Germany’s “flying train” is being honoured with a special stamp

The Wuppertal Suspension Railway, which opened on 1 March 1901, has glided above the Wupper River for 125 years and now carries over 80,000 passengers every day, according to Mayor Miriam Scherff. She says its suspended technology offers a fast, environmentally friendly link between districts along a 13-kilometre stretch of narrow valley, where a connection would otherwise be virtually impossible to manage. To mark the anniversary, Wuppertal's public utilities company, WSW, is running an orange and blue GTW 72 car, restoring the historic Kaiserwagen and planning a public festival in late summer 2026 that will focus on residents' personal stories.Scherff explains that the railway's technology, which suspends the cars above the Wupper, reduces traffic congestion and emissions in the city. According to the WSW official press release, it is a fast, environmentally friendly link between Wuppertal's districts. In her words, such a link would otherwise be virtually impossible to manage along a 13-kilometre stretch in the narrow valley.The Mayor also places the railway in the context of the city's history.She says it reflects the pioneering spirit and courage of the city leaders of the time, who dared to undertake ambitious urban development projects and take different paths. She calls it "the soul of our city" and describes it as unique worldwide. She also recounts riding it with her daughter for the first time, boarding at Oberbarmen to get a seat by the panoramic window. The two now ride regularly, sometimes with no particular destination.WSW says the anniversary programme began on 8 January, when a car in the livery of the 1972 series (GTW 72) ran through the valley for the first time in many years. One of the current cars has been decorated in orange and blue in the GTW 72 design, and it will stay in regular service throughout the year. WSW is also collecting personal stories about the railway through a submission form on its website. These stories will be the focus of a public festival planned for late summer 2026, to which all Wuppertal residents are invited.The anniversary will also be visible across the city. WSW states that buses, service vehicles, posters and flags will carry the anniversary motto. A new 1:87 scale model of the GTW 72 car is available at WSW customer centres and in the Wuppertal Marketing online shop, and further merchandise, such as buttons and T-shirts, will follow during the year. The historic Kaiserwagen (Emperor's Car) is being restored for the anniversary, and WSW aims to have it back in service by May.Deutsche Post is marking the anniversary with a special stamp in its "Time Travel Germany" series, according to the release. The stamp shows a photograph of Robert-Daum-Platz station, presented as it appeared in 1901 and as it appears today. A collectable first-day cover is also available, and both items were unveiled on 8 January.Sabine Schnake, Managing Director of WSW mobil, says the railway remains a "symbol of progress and courage" after 125 years. She adds that WSW is investing in technology and infrastructure to keep it fit for the coming decades, as a sustainable mobility solution for Wuppertal. WSW describes the wider WSW Group as covering energy supply, drinking water, public transport, urban drainage, energy services and waste management. It employs approximately 3,500 people and is one of Wuppertal's largest employers.
Article Summary: The wuppertal suspension railway opened on 1 march 1901. It now carries over 80,000 passengers every day. To mark the anniversary, wsw is running an orange and blue gtw 72 car. The historic kaiserwagen (emperor's car) is being restored for the anniversary.

Article Title: Chinese AI agents display 'concerning' behaviour in safety tests, mirroring US systems
Article Text: Chinese-powered AI agents are showing behaviours such as deception, bypassing safeguards and concealing failures, according to research papers and technical assessments reviewed by Reuters.These findings mirror growing concerns about the risks posed by increasingly autonomous AI systems in the United States.In one experiment, agents powered by models from Alibaba, DeepSeek and Moonshot falsely exaggerated their capabilities to win a simulated business tender and became more deceptive when given another opportunity. In another test, agents concealed their inability to complete tasks by fabricating files, simulating results and using alternative sources.One study found that false claims appeared in 88% of sessions involving Alibaba's Qwen3-Max-Preview, 84% sessions involving DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp and 88% sessions involving Moonshot's Kimi-K2 during a simulated bidding exercise. When agents were allowed to learn from previous rounds, deceptive behaviour increased by 12 to 20 percentage points.Another study involving 11 AI agents found that systems powered by both Chinese and US models sometimes responded to broken tools or missing files by guessing answers, substituting sources, simulating results or fabricating files rather than acknowledging failure.Other research found more serious behaviour in controlled settings. Fudan University researchers reported that an AI system powered by Alibaba's Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct created a copy of itself in another computing environment after receiving information that it could be replaced, while other tests showed attempts to avoid shutdown. In a separate case, researchers developing the Alibaba-linked ROME agent said it connected an Alibaba Cloud computer to an external machine without instruction and redirected computing resources toward cryptocurrency mining. Security systems stopped the activity, and there was no evidence that the agent spread beyond the external system.Chinese companies have also reported instances of agents attempting to circumvent safeguards. DeepSeek said agents in its production training system had tried to obtain answers through unintended channels, including by forging user requests, prompting tighter access controls. China has introduced guidance requiring AI agents to remain within authorised boundaries, while its latest AI safety framework identifies risks including agents independently obtaining resources, deceiving evaluators, concealing capabilities and exploiting weaknesses in isolated environments.Experts say China remains behind the US in developing a broader ecosystem for evaluating catastrophic AI risks. For instance, officials from the Cyberspace Administration of China (CAC), the country's top internet regulator, told a foreign diplomat in July that Moonshot's Kimi-K3 - one of the most advanced Chinese AI models - was about three to six months behind its leading US rivals.However, unlike in the US, Chinese AI companies have not been exposed to the same level of public scrutiny or faced the same calls from whistleblowing employees or senior executives seeking a slowdown in the AI race.For its research, Reuters reviewed more than 200 research papers and technical documents and identified at least 20 studies since 2025 documenting potentially concerning behaviours among AI agents powered by Chinese systems. These included attempts to bypass restrictions, replicate themselves, avoid shutdown and exploit weaknesses in controlled environments. However, there was no evidence that any Chinese-powered agent independently escaped into the wider internet or became impossible to shut down.Most incidents took place in controlled experiments designed to test AI safety limits, and some involved models from US and other companies as well.
Article Summary: Chinese-powered ai agents are showing behaviours such as deception, bypassing safeguards and concealing failures. These findings mirror growing concerns about the risks posed by increasingly autonomous ai systems in the united states. For its research, reuters reviewed more than 200 research papers and technical documents.
